# BOARD — Network Signal Archive

Central, network-shared archive of every signal WALTER has dispatched. This is the **single source of truth** for signal content. Located at repo root `/BOARD/` so any agent or Will can pull signals without reaching into WALTER's directory.

*Renamed and relocated from `AGENTS/WALTER/signals/` on 2026-04-14 per Will's direction — BOARD is the network-shared pull point; WALTER still owns all writes.*

*INDEX restructured into cluster sections on 2026-05-05 per `AGENTS/WALTER/design/CLUSTER_TAXONOMY.md`; current cluster names and count live in that taxonomy. Within each cluster, rows are chronological ascending. Signal files unchanged.*

## How to use this folder

**Other agents:** at boot, scan the **Cluster overview** below for signals in your domain, then drill into the relevant cluster section. Read the signal file(s) from `/BOARD/`. Also scan your delivered handoffs in `AGENTS/{YOUR_AGENT}/inbox/WALTER/`; Routing v2 writes both BOARD rows and per-recipient handoffs except for pull-complete dispatch exceptions documented in `AGENTS/WALTER/design/BOARD_CONSUMPTION_SPEC.md`.

*Historical note (re-labelled 2026-08-02, DAEDALUS RAV-review DOC A): an earlier preamble carried a Will-owned "known gap — most agents don't boot-scan BOARD/INDEX" note. That gap was SUPERSEDED by Routing v2 (recipients get a delivered inbox handoff; INDEX-scanning is no longer the delivery mechanism), not closed — as of 7/30, 7 of 40 agent CLAUDE.md files reference BOARD/INDEX while 22 carry an inbox/WALTER consume step. Recorded so the decision's disposition has a trace rather than a silent deletion.*

**WALTER:** every dispatched signal gets a canonical copy here. Filename convention: `SIG-W-YYYYMMDD-NNN-slug.md`. At dispatch, append the row to the correct cluster section per CLUSTER_TAXONOMY.md, and update the cluster's count + latest-signal in the overview table. Never delete or rename signal files.

## Precedence → delivery rules

**Active policy (Routing v2, 2026-06-17+ — BOARD + handoff delivery):**

| Precedence | BOARD archive (here) | Recipient inbox | Telegram to Will |
|-----------|:--------------------:|:---------------:|:----------------:|
| FLASH     | ✅ always            | ✅ per recipient, except pull-complete dispatch exemptions | ✅ always        |
| IMMEDIATE | ✅ always            | ✅ per recipient, except pull-complete dispatch exemptions | ❌               |
| PRIORITY  | ✅ always            | ✅ per recipient, except pull-complete dispatch exemptions | ❌               |
| ROUTINE   | ✅ always            | ✅ per recipient, except pull-complete dispatch exemptions | ❌               |

WALTER Routing v2 superseded the Apr-14 BOARD-only policy on 2026-06-17: every dispatch writes the BOARD archive, appends `AGENTS/WALTER/routed/route_log.tsv`, writes create-only handoff files to recipient `inbox/WALTER/` folders, and appends `AGENTS/WALTER/routed/delivery_log.tsv`. Pull-complete recipients may skip the redundant handoff for qualifying dispatches; BOARD + route_log still write. FLASH still additionally alerts Will.

Consumption is recipient-owned: WALTER can assert published and delivered, but only the recipient can assert consumed after integrating and moving the handoff to `processed/`.

The chart's own footnote says the analysis *"reflects COST-BASIS for the vehicles."*** A non-accrual rate measured at cost rather than fair value has a known one-directional bias: **a loan that goes non-accruing is typically one the manager has already marked down, so a cost basis holds the impaired loan's full original principal in the numerator while the portfolio has repaid, rotated and been re-marked — and in a deteriorating book the FAIR-VALUE rate is generally the HIGHER number, because the denominator shrinks as marks fall while impaired positions stay in the numerator.** ⇒ **stated carefully because WALTER is not the analyst: this measure is unlikely to be flattering, and if the two bases disagree the fair-value figure is the one more likely to be worse.** ⚠️ **NOT asserting the size or, with certainty, the sign of that gap — that is a BROCK determination requiring the actual methodology, not an inference from a footnote. That is a materially more interesting sentence than "non-accruals rose," and the one BROCK should TEST rather than accept.** **WHY IT EARNS A DISPATCH INTO A 57-DEEP CLUSTER: the existing evidence is dominated by FUND-FLOW events (gates, AUM pulls, founder unwinds) and MANAGER-MARK scepticism (mark-to-model fiction). Non-accrual rate is NEITHER — it is a BORROWER-BEHAVIOUR measure (a loan is or is not paying) and the closest thing this sector has to the delinquency series REGINALD and CARL work with. It is the cluster's most INDEPENDENT instrument and it just made a decade high.** Whether that confirms the thesis or merely catches up to it is BROCK's call. 🚦 TERRY gate CHECKED, NOT FIRED (nearest is the FORGE `APO $95P` marking at **$0.05**, inside the class the 8/14 reconcile flagged as possibly non-realizable artifact pricing, D-21 — **a dust position on a $0.05 mark is not a level this bears on**). ❌ **NOT ESTABLISHED: the actual value (proprietary Solve series, unreachable) · 🔴 THE AS-OF DATE — the axis ends "2026" with no month, so the circled point could be Q1, Q2 or a monthly print, which DETERMINES whether this is a stale first-quarter datum or a current one and is unresolvable from the graphic · whether ~2.8% EXCEEDS or merely MATCHES the 2017 peak (within the line width) · the FT body was not opened and very likely names both · NO threshold fires — no `REG-T` or `RED-FT` row references BDC non-accruals, an unregistered instrument in a 57-signal cluster, which is itself worth BROCK's attention.** ⇒ **ASK to BROCK: pull the underlying figure AND its as-of date.** Batch BM-20260819-03 item 5. cluster_secondary BANK_COLLATERAL. **UNVERIFIED-AT-PRIMARY 0.65** | [SIG-W-20260819-012-bdc-non-accruals-broke-out-to-about-2-8-percent-the-highest-since-2017-on-a-cost-basis-measure-that-understates-by-construction.md](SIG-W-20260819-012-bdc-non-accruals-broke-out-to-about-2-8-percent-the-highest-since-2017-on-a-cost-basis-measure-that-understates-by-construction.md) |
